run.procedureSummary: 1. Charge: add each cycle's charge to crucibles 1 to 6. Overfill is allowed at this step. 2. Overflow: go from 1 to 6 in order. If a crucible holds more than its working volume, the excess moves into the next crucible before that crucible's turn. Excess from 6 goes to slag. 3. State: a BASE crucible at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. A SUPERHEATED crucible at or below its lower mark becomes BASE. Otherwise the state stays the same. Every change is logged. 4. Bleed: all six amounts are worked out from the contents after overflow, rounded down, before anything moves. BASE loses floor(q/4) to slag. SUPERHEATED sends floor(q/2) to the crucible before it (from 1 it goes to slag). Any overfill this causes is left in place until the next cycle's overflow step. After cycle 5 it stays. 5. Emergency tap: if the total across all six is strictly greater than 38, each crucible keeps floor(q/2) and the rest goes to slag.

openPoints.point: Whether the state check at step 3 uses the contents after overflow
openPoints.assumption: Yes. Steps run in order, so step 3 sees the contents after step 2.

openPoints.point: Whether a crucible's own bleed amount is based on contents that include what it receives from the crucible after it
openPoints.assumption: No. All six amounts are worked out from the contents before any move ('figure all six ... then move'). A crucible's bleed comes only from its own pre-bleed contents.

openPoints.point: Rounding of the bleed and of the tap halving
openPoints.assumption: Bleed amounts are rounded down. In the tap, each crucible keeps floor(q/2) and the remainder, ceil(q/2), goes to slag.
'Over 38' means strictly greater than 38. A total of exactly 38, as at the end of cycle 5, does not fire the tap.

openPoints.point: When the tap test is applied
openPoints.assumption: After the bleed, using the total of all six crucibles.

openPoints.point: Overflow from a crucible that has already had its turn
openPoints.assumption: Overflow is a single pass from 1 to 6. Excess sent forward is checked when the next crucible's turn comes. Nothing flows backward during overflow.

run.balanceCheck: Starting melt 20 + all charges 94 = 114. End melt 38 + slag tally 76 = 114. Balanced.
run.notes: I ran a short Python script for the arithmetic. It is in the session scratchpad as crucible.py, not in the repo. I did not commit anything. The repo's pre-registered plan (openmirror/evidence/transformation-2026-10-07/compression-250/PLAN.md) shows this run is one blind read in the 250-word compression test. Under that plan, reads are collected by the workflow and the results go into RESULTS.md and verify.py. A reader committing its own result would step outside that procedure, so the commit is left to the orchestrating workflow. The tap fired in cycles 1 and 4. At the end of cycle 5 the total was exactly 38, which is not over 38, so the tap did not fire.
